title: Abbott i-STAT 1 Blood Gas Analyzer - Cartridge Not Recognized or Insertion Errors
description: Troubleshooting cartridge recognition and insertion errors caused by seating, damage, or contact issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot while actively testing a patient sample. Use a backup analyzer if immediate testing is required.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Insert a cartridge and observe for 'Cartridge not recognized', no response, or repeated prompts to confirm the issue is reproducible.

steps.title: Check Cartridge Compatibility and Expiration (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Confirm correct cartridge type, check expiration date, and verify proper storage conditions.

steps.title: Inspect Cartridge for Physical Damage or Contamination
steps.instructions: Check for cracks, bent contacts, debris, or fluid contamination on cartridge contacts.

steps.title: Verify Proper Cartridge Insertion Technique
steps.instructions: Ensure cartridge is fully seated, properly aligned, and inserted without angling.

steps.title: Inspect Analyzer Cartridge Port (High-Value Check)
steps.instructions: Check for debris, contamination, or damaged pins inside the cartridge port and clean if needed.

steps.title: Perform Analyzer Restart
steps.instructions: Power off, wait 10–15 seconds, then power on and retest.

steps.title: Test with a Known-Good Cartridge
steps.instructions: Use a cartridge from a different lot or verified stock to rule out batch issues.

CCR.Complaint: Analyzer not recognizing cartridges during blood gas testing.
CCR.Cause: Expired and improperly stored cartridges failed to establish contact.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced with in-date cartridges stored per guidelines; analyzer function restored.

helpfulDetails: Alarm behavior or error messages observed

title: Abbott i-STAT 1 Blood Gas Analyzer - Analyzer Lockout or QC Failures
description: Troubleshooting analyzer lockout or QC failures on the Abbott i-STAT 1 due to quality control, cartridge, or configuration-related issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot while the analyzer is needed for active patient testing. Move testing to a backup analyzer if available.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Lockout or QC Failure
steps.instructions: Power on the analyzer and review the display. Confirm lockout message or QC failure notification, note any specific error messages or codes, and attempt to access testing mode.

steps.title: Check Operator ID and Authorization Settings (Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Verify operator ID is entered correctly, confirm operator certification status if required, and try a known authorized operator ID.

steps.title: Verify Quality Control (QC) Requirements
steps.instructions: Check QC status in the analyzer menu, confirm QC has been performed within the required timeframe, and review the last QC result.

steps.title: Perform Required QC Test
steps.instructions: Use appropriate QC material, ensure cartridges are within expiration and stored properly, and run QC per facility protocol.

steps.title: Inspect Test Cartridges (Frequent Contributor to QC Failure)
steps.instructions: Check expiration dates, confirm proper storage conditions, allow cartridges to reach room temperature, and try a new cartridge from a different lot.

steps.title: Check Analyzer Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Ensure proper operating temperature, avoid drafts or sunlight, and allow the device to acclimate if recently moved.

steps.title: Inspect Analyzer Contacts and Cartridge Port
steps.instructions: Inspect the cartridge port for debris, ensure contacts are clean and dry, and avoid inserting damaged cartridges.

steps.title: Perform Analyzer Reset
steps.instructions: Power off the analyzer, remove batteries if applicable, restart, and reattempt QC.

CCR.Complaint: Analyzer locked out and unable to run patient tests due to QC failure.
CCR.Cause: Expired QC requirement and failed QC due to outdated cartridge lot.
CCR.Resolution: Performed QC with new cartridge, passed QC, and restored analyzer to service.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (returned to service or removed)

title: Abbott i-STAT 1 Blood Gas Analyzer - Wireless Download or Connectivity Failure
description: Troubleshooting wireless transmission failures, connectivity issues, and docking-related download problems on the Abbott i-STAT 1 analyzer.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot while the analyzer is actively being used for patient testing. Complete testing or switch to another device first.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Connectivity Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to transmit results or connect to the system. Confirm presence or absence of wireless connection indicators and check for failed transmission messages or missing results in LIS/EMR.

steps.title: Check Wireless Signal Availability (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Move the device closer to a known access point or docking station and check signal strength indicator if available.

steps.title: Verify Analyzer Wireless Settings
steps.instructions: Access device settings/menu, confirm wireless is enabled, and verify correct network profile is selected.

steps.title: Check Docking Station or Base Unit (If Used)
steps.instructions: Ensure dock has power, confirm network cable is connected if applicable, and reseat analyzer in dock.

steps.title: Inspect for Physical or Environmental Interference
steps.instructions: Look for nearby equipment causing interference, avoid metal cabinets or shielded rooms, and confirm no visible antenna damage.

steps.title: Restart the Analyzer
steps.instructions: Turn the device off and back on, then attempt transmission again.

steps.title: Test with Known-Good Network or Dock
steps.instructions: Try connecting in a different known working area or dock and compare with another i-STAT device.

CCR.Complaint: Analyzer not transmitting results wirelessly to the system.
CCR.Cause: Weak wireless signal and improper docking station connection.
CCR.Resolution: Moved device to proper coverage area, reseated in powered dock, and verified successful transmission.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (operational or removed from service)

title: Abbott i-STAT 1 Blood Gas Analyzer - Battery Not Charging or Shortened Runtime
description: Troubleshooting battery charging issues, short runtime, and unexpected shutdowns on the Abbott i-STAT 1 analyzer.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot while the analyzer is actively being used for patient testing. Move testing to a backup device.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to power the unit and place it in the charger/docking station. Observe for no charging indicator, rapid battery drain, or unexpected shutdown.

steps.title: Check Charging Station Power (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Confirm outlet is working, check power adapter connection, and verify dock indicator lights.

steps.title: Inspect Analyzer Seating in Dock
steps.instructions: Reseat the analyzer, ensure correct orientation, and check for obstructions preventing contact.

steps.title: Inspect Charging Contacts (Common Issue)
steps.instructions: Check for dirt or corrosion, clean contacts, and verify they are not damaged.

steps.title: Test with Known-Good Charger or Dock
steps.instructions: Place the analyzer in a confirmed working dock to isolate whether the issue is with the dock or analyzer.

steps.title: Evaluate Battery Performance
steps.instructions: Fully charge the unit, remove it, and monitor runtime to assess battery condition.

steps.title: Perform Power Cycle / Reset
steps.instructions: Turn the unit off and restart to clear minor faults.

CCR.Complaint: i-STAT 1 analyzer not charging and shutting down quickly during use.
CCR.Cause: Worn battery with reduced capacity and poor charging contact.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned contacts, tested with known-good dock, and removed unit from service for battery replacement.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (in service vs out of service)

title: Abbott i-STAT 1 Blood Gas Analyzer - Display or Keypad Failure
description: Unresponsive keypad, blank or dim screen, or incorrect display behavior caused by battery, contamination, or external damage.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot while the analyzer is needed for active patient testing. Move testing to another analyzer.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Power on the analyzer and attempt normal operation. Observe: Blank or dim screen, Partial display or distorted text, Keypad buttons not responding or delayed response

steps.title: Check Battery Condition (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Low or unstable battery power can cause display and keypad malfunctions. Remove and reseat the battery. Replace with a known-good, fully charged battery

steps.title: Inspect for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Examine the screen and keypad for visible issues. Check for cracks, impact damage, or worn keypad buttons. Look for signs of fluid intrusion

steps.title: Check for Contamination (Very Common in POC Devices)
steps.instructions: Residue from gloves, fluids, or cleaning agents can affect keypad responsiveness. Inspect keypad for sticky or unresponsive buttons. Clean surface using approved disinfectant wipes (per facility policy). Allow device to fully dry before retesting

steps.title: Perform a Power Reset
steps.instructions: Resetting the device can clear temporary faults. Power off the analyzer. Remove battery for 30–60 seconds. Reinstall battery and power back on

steps.title: Check Operating Environment
steps.instructions: Environmental factors can impact display visibility and keypad performance. Verify device is within normal temperature range. Avoid direct bright light affecting screen visibility

CCR.Complaint: Analyzer display blank and keypad unresponsive during blood gas testing.
CCR.Cause: Battery voltage low causing improper display and input function.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced battery with known-good unit; device returned to normal operation.

helpfulDetails: Signs of contamination or fluid exposure

title: Abbott Precision Xceed Pro Blood Glucose Meter - Strip Not Recognized or Insertion Errors
description: Troubleshooting when test strips are not detected, improperly inserted, or causing repeated read errors due to external factors.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the device from patient use if testing is delayed or unreliable. Use an alternate meter if needed.

steps.title: Verify Correct Strip Type
steps.instructions: Confirm the strips being used are compatible with the Precision Xceed Pro (glucose vs ketone strips). Check strip vial labeling and ensure strips match device capability.

steps.title: Inspect Strip Orientation and Insertion Technique
steps.instructions: Ensure the strip is inserted fully and in the correct direction. Insert strip firmly until it stops and confirm contact end is inserted first.

steps.title: Check Strip Condition and Expiration
steps.instructions: Inspect strips for damage, contamination, or expiration. Check expiration date on vial and inspect for bent, dirty, or exposed strips.

steps.title: Inspect the Strip Port for Contamination
steps.instructions: Look for debris, dried blood, or residue inside the strip port. Visually inspect port using a light and gently clean using approved method.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Device
steps.instructions: Restart the meter to clear any temporary recognition errors. Turn device off and back on, then reinsert strip after reboot.

steps.title: Test with a New Strip from a Different Lot (If Available)
steps.instructions: Rule out defective strip batch by using a strip from a new vial or different lot.

steps.title: Observe for Repeated Failures or Intermittent Detection
steps.instructions: Determine if the issue is consistent across multiple attempts. Consistent failure suggests device issue while intermittent detection may indicate worn contacts.

CCR.Complaint: Meter not recognizing test strips during patient glucose testing.
CCR.Cause: Contamination found in strip port preventing proper strip contact.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned strip port and verified proper operation with new test strip.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (returned to service or sent for repair)

title: Abbott Precision Xceed Pro Blood Glucose Meter - QC Lockout or Control Failures
description: Troubleshooting QC lockout, failed control tests, or meter preventing patient testing due to quality control requirements or invalid QC results.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not delay patient care due to meter lockout. Move testing to another verified meter if needed.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Lockout or Failure
steps.instructions: Check the display for messages such as QC required, QC failed, or lockout active.

steps.title: Check QC Requirements and Timing Settings
steps.instructions: Verify if the meter requires daily QC, QC after strip lot change, or QC after maintenance or battery replacement. Review facility policy if needed.

steps.title: Inspect Control Solution (Most Common Cause)
steps.instructions: Check the control solution for expiration date, open vial date, and proper storage conditions.

steps.title: Check Test Strips
steps.instructions: Verify correct strip type, expiration, storage conditions, and lot compatibility.

steps.title: Perform QC Test Correctly
steps.instructions: Repeat QC using proper technique including mixing control solution, applying correct drop size, avoiding contamination, and following prompts.

steps.title: Compare QC Results to Acceptable Range
steps.instructions: Check that results fall within the range printed on the strip vial or control insert.

steps.title: Try a New Bottle of Control Solution and New Strip Vial
steps.instructions: Open a new control solution and use a new vial of strips if QC continues to fail.

steps.title: Check Meter Cleanliness and Strip Port Condition
steps.instructions: Inspect for residue or debris and clean per manufacturer-approved method.

steps.title: Power Cycle the Meter
steps.instructions: Turn the meter off and back on or reseat the battery if applicable.

CCR.Complaint: Meter in ED locked out due to repeated QC failures and unable to perform patient testing.
CCR.Cause: Expired control solution and degraded test strip vial causing out-of-range QC results.
CCR.Resolution: Replaced control solution and test strips, performed QC successfully, and returned meter to service.

helpfulDetails: Control solution expiration and open date verified
QC results (in or out of range)
Final device status (returned to service or removed)

title: Abbott Precision Xceed Pro Blood Glucose Meter - Connectivity or Data Transfer Failure
description: Failure to upload results, sync data, or communicate with docking station or data management system due to connection, configuration, or accessory issues.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Do not delay patient care while troubleshooting connectivity. Use another meter if results are needed urgently.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to upload data or dock the meter and observe behavior. Check for no upload activity, error messages, or dock not recognizing meter.

steps.title: Check Docking Station Power and Status
steps.instructions: Verify power cable is plugged in, confirm outlet is working, and observe LED indicators on dock.

steps.title: Inspect Physical Connections
steps.instructions: Reseat Ethernet/USB cables, look for damaged or loose connectors, and try a known-good cable if available.

steps.title: Clean Meter and Dock Contacts
steps.instructions: Inspect for debris, residue, or corrosion, clean contacts with approved wipes, and allow to dry fully.

steps.title: Verify Proper Meter Docking
steps.instructions: Remove and reseat the meter and confirm it sits firmly and evenly.

steps.title: Check Network Availability (if applicable)
steps.instructions: Check network port status lights and verify other devices on same network are functioning.

steps.title: Restart the Meter
steps.instructions: Turn the meter off, wait 10–15 seconds, turn it back on, and retry upload.

steps.title: Try a Different Docking Station (if available)
steps.instructions: Test the meter in another known-good dock to determine if the issue is meter-related or dock-related.

steps.title: Check Date/Time Settings
steps.instructions: Verify the meter’s date and time are correct.

CCR.Complaint: Meter would not upload results when placed in docking station.
CCR.Cause: Dirty communication contacts preventing proper docking connection.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned meter and dock contacts; verified successful data transfer.

helpfulDetails: Dock powered and LED status confirmed

title: Abbott Precision Xceed Pro Blood Glucose Meter - Battery or Power Failure
description: Troubleshooting a meter that will not power on, shuts off unexpectedly, or shows low battery despite charging or battery replacement.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety First
steps.instructions: Remove the meter from patient use and obtain a backup device before troubleshooting.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Attempt to power on the device and observe for no response, intermittent shutdown, or low battery indicator.

steps.title: Check Battery Installation (Most Common Issue)
steps.instructions: Remove and reinsert the batteries, ensuring correct orientation and proper seating.

steps.title: Inspect Battery Contacts
steps.instructions: Check for dirt, corrosion, or bent contacts and clean gently if needed using approved methods.

steps.title: Replace with Known Good Batteries
steps.instructions: Install new manufacturer-recommended batteries and avoid mixing old and new batteries.

steps.title: Check Battery Compartment Door
steps.instructions: Ensure the battery cover is fully closed and latched.

steps.title: Inspect for Physical Damage
steps.instructions: Check for cracks, fluid intrusion, or signs of impact damage.

steps.title: Perform a Power Reset
steps.instructions: Remove batteries, wait 30–60 seconds, then reinstall.

CCR.Complaint: Nursing reported Precision Xceed Pro would not power on during glucose testing.
CCR.Cause: Battery contacts found corroded, preventing proper electrical connection.
CCR.Resolution: Cleaned contacts and installed new batteries; device powered on and passed functional check.

helpfulDetails: Final device status (returned to service or sent for repair)

title: Abbott Precision Xceed Pro Blood Glucose Meter - Display or Keypad Malfunction
description: Unresponsive buttons, frozen screen, dim display, or incorrect input preventing normal operation or patient testing.

steps.title: Ensure Patient Safety
steps.instructions: Do not troubleshoot while the device is in use on a patient. Move testing to a known working meter.

steps.title: Verify the Reported Issue
steps.instructions: Power on the device and attempt to use multiple buttons. Check for no response to key presses, delayed or inconsistent response, frozen screen or partial display.

steps.title: Check Battery Status
steps.instructions: Inspect battery level indicator on the screen. Replace batteries with known good ones and ensure proper battery orientation.

steps.title: Perform a Full Power Reset
steps.instructions: Remove batteries completely, wait 30–60 seconds, reinstall batteries and power on.

steps.title: Inspect Keypad for Physical Obstruction or Damage
steps.instructions: Check buttons for sticky residue, physical damage or wear, and buttons stuck in pressed position.

steps.title: Clean External Surfaces
steps.instructions: Using approved cleaning wipes, clean keypad and screen surface and allow device to fully dry before testing again.

steps.title: Check Display Visibility
steps.instructions: Inspect screen for cracks or internal damage, faded, dim, or missing segments, and backlight failure.

steps.title: Test with Known Good Dock or Accessories (if applicable)
steps.instructions: Remove from dock and test independently. Try a different dock if available.

steps.title: Attempt Basic Function Navigation
steps.instructions: Try navigating menus or performing a control test (without patient sample).

CCR.Complaint: Device display frozen and keypad not responding during glucose testing.
CCR.Cause: Internal keypad/display failure after external checks and battery replacement.
CCR.Resolution: Removed from service and sent for repair; replacement meter issued to unit.

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Analyzer Will Not Power On or Complete Initialization
description: Addresses no-power, incomplete startup, or initialization failures caused by external power, connections, accessories, environmental conditions, or recoverable startup conditions.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Testing and Confirm Analyzer Status
steps.instructions: Stop relying on the Alinity hq for patient testing until normal operation is verified. Route specimens to another validated analyzer or follow the laboratory's approved downtime process. Confirm exactly what staff observed: completely dead, powers on but stops during startup, repeatedly restarts, displays a message, or remains in a not-ready state. Expected outcome: Patient testing continues through an alternate workflow, and the exact failure condition is identified. If the analyzer subsequently initializes normally and passes required verification, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 2. Inspect for Obvious Hazards
steps.instructions: Inspect the analyzer and surrounding area for liquid spills, damaged cords, loose panels, unusual odor, overheating, smoke, abnormal noise, or evidence of recent impact or service. Do not continue powering the analyzer if an electrical, mechanical, or fluid hazard is present. Expected outcome: No condition is found that makes continued troubleshooting unsafe. If damage, overheating, or another hazard is present, remove the analyzer from service and stop troubleshooting.

steps.title: 3. Verify External Power
steps.instructions: Confirm the analyzer's external power connection is fully seated and the power cord is not damaged, pinched, or loose. Verify the connected receptacle or approved power source is functioning using an appropriate method. Check whether nearby equipment lost power or whether facilities work, breaker activity, UPS events, or outlet changes occurred around the time of failure. Expected outcome: A stable external power source is confirmed. If restoring a loose connection or correcting the approved external power source allows normal startup, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify Required External Connections
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible external cables and peripheral connections used during startup. Confirm plugs are fully seated and no cable has been pulled, crushed, or inadvertently disconnected. Do not disconnect unidentified cables or alter network infrastructure without confirming their purpose. Expected outcome: Required external connections are secure and undamaged. If reseating an approved external connection restores initialization, complete functional verification and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Analyzer Covers, Doors, and Accessible Components
steps.instructions: Verify accessible covers, doors, reagent areas, sample-loading areas, waste connections, and other operator-accessible assemblies are properly closed and seated. Look for anything physically preventing a cover, drawer, or carrier mechanism from reaching its normal position. Expected outcome: All externally accessible assemblies are properly positioned. If correcting an obvious obstruction permits initialization to complete, verify ready status and stop.

steps.title: 6. Review the Displayed Startup Condition
steps.instructions: Document any exact message, status indication, or initialization stage shown by the analyzer. Determine whether the analyzer is waiting for an external condition such as consumables, waste handling, fluid availability, temperature stabilization, or a connected subsystem. Do not bypass interlocks or enter restricted service functions. Expected outcome: Any externally correctable startup condition is identified and corrected. If the analyzer reaches normal ready status afterward, troubleshooting can stop following required verification.

steps.title: 7. Perform an Approved Restart if Appropriate
steps.instructions: If no hazard is present and laboratory workflow permits, perform a normal shutdown and restart using the approved operating controls. Avoid repeated power cycling. Observe whether startup progresses farther, fails at the same point, or produces a consistent message. Expected outcome: The analyzer completes initialization and reaches normal operating status. If the same failure repeats, continue to escalation rather than repeatedly restarting.

steps.title: 8. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: After the analyzer initializes, verify normal ready indications and basic system operation. Confirm required laboratory quality checks are satisfactory before releasing patient results. Expected outcome: The analyzer starts normally and required operational and quality verification passes. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the Abbott Alinity hq powered on but would not complete initialization.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an accessible external connection partially unseated, preventing normal startup.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the connection, restarted the analyzer normally, confirmed initialization completed, and verified the analyzer returned to an appropriate ready state for laboratory quality checks.

helpfulDetails: Whether the analyzer was completely dead or partially initialized
Recent power, facilities, or network work
Unusual odor, heat, sound, or visible damage
Quality-verification result before return to use

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Barcode, LIS, or Network Communication Fails
description: Addresses barcode, LIS, and network failures caused by label quality, cabling, connectivity, interface status, configuration, or external infrastructure problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Identification and Result Routing
steps.instructions: Do not manually associate specimens or transmit results outside approved laboratory downtime procedures when identification or interface communication is unreliable. Confirm whether the issue affects barcode reading, worklist receipt, order matching, result transmission, or all network communication. Expected outcome: Patient identification and result integrity are protected, and the affected communication layer is identified.

steps.title: 2. Determine the Scope
steps.instructions: Check whether one sample barcode fails or all barcodes fail. Determine whether one analyzer is affected or other laboratory systems are also experiencing LIS or network problems. Expected outcome: The problem is identified as sample-specific, analyzer-specific, or infrastructure-wide.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Barcode
steps.instructions: For sample-specific failures, inspect the barcode for wrinkles, smearing, low contrast, damage, excessive curvature, poor placement, or obstruction by another label. Use a known-good properly labeled sample or approved test barcode for comparison. Expected outcome: A valid barcode is read successfully. If only the original label fails, correct the specimen-identification issue and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect External Network Connections
steps.instructions: Verify accessible network or interface cables are fully seated and not damaged. Check link indicators where normally visible without disturbing infrastructure. Do not move cables between network ports unless the approved port assignment is known. Expected outcome: Physical communication connections are secure. If reseating an approved loose connection restores communication, verify end-to-end transmission and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Analyzer Communication Status
steps.instructions: Review the normal analyzer interface or connectivity status available to Clinical Engineering and laboratory staff. Determine whether the analyzer reports disconnected, offline, paused, or another visible communication state. Expected outcome: The analyzer is configured to participate in normal communication. If communication was simply paused and approved restoration resolves the issue, verify and stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify the Upstream and Downstream Path
steps.instructions: Determine whether the LIS, middleware, interface engine, switch, or other connected systems are available. Coordinate with laboratory IT or hospital IT when appropriate. Avoid changing IP addressing, ports, interface configuration, or routing without an approved change process. Expected outcome: External infrastructure availability is confirmed, or the issue is appropriately transferred to the responsible team.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Other Connected Devices
steps.instructions: Check whether another laboratory analyzer on the same workflow can receive orders and send results. A broader outage suggests network, LIS, middleware, or interface infrastructure rather than an isolated Alinity hq failure. Expected outcome: The fault domain is narrowed to the analyzer or shared infrastructure.

steps.title: 8. Review Recent Changes
steps.instructions: Ask whether the issue began after switch work, network maintenance, LIS changes, middleware updates, analyzer relocation, cable work, or configuration changes. Document the timing and involved teams. Expected outcome: A recent external change is identified or ruled out.

steps.title: 9. Perform an Approved Communication Restart
steps.instructions: If appropriate and coordinated with the laboratory, restart the normal communication session or perform an approved analyzer restart. Do not repeatedly reboot to compensate for unresolved infrastructure problems. Expected outcome: Communication reconnects and remains stable. If it does, proceed to end-to-end verification.

steps.title: 10. Verify the Complete Communication Path
steps.instructions: Using an approved test workflow, confirm sample identification, order receipt where applicable, analysis association, result transmission, and receipt at the intended downstream system. Expected outcome: Barcode and LIS/network communication function correctly end to end. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the Abbott Alinity hq completed testing but results were not transmitting to the LIS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the analyzer's external network cable partially disconnected at the approved connection point.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering secured the network connection and verified a test result transmitted successfully through the laboratory interface to the intended downstream system.

helpfulDetails: Whether barcode, orders, results, or all communication failed
One sample or all samples affected

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Calibration Fails or Will Not Complete
description: Addresses failed or incomplete calibration caused by material condition, preparation, aspiration, environmental conditions, analyzer readiness, or unresolved quality issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Results
steps.instructions: Do not report patient results from affected parameters when required calibration is incomplete or unacceptable. Follow the laboratory's approved alternate-testing process. Confirm which calibration activity failed and whether the failure is consistent or intermittent. Expected outcome: Result integrity is protected and the specific calibration failure is identified.

steps.title: 2. Review the Exact Calibration Failure
steps.instructions: Record the exact analyzer message, parameter, point in the calibration process, and whether the run stopped or completed unsuccessfully. Do not immediately repeat calibration without first checking likely external causes. Expected outcome: A reproducible calibration condition is documented.

steps.title: 3. Verify Calibration Material
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct calibration material is being used and that its laboratory-controlled identification, storage, handling, and preparation are appropriate. Inspect for contamination, leakage, improper mixing, or insufficient volume. Expected outcome: Calibration material is suitable for use. If material condition is questionable, replace it with appropriate material before proceeding.

steps.title: 4. Verify Sample Presentation
steps.instructions: Check that the calibration material container is correctly loaded, properly positioned, and compatible with the validated laboratory workflow. Inspect labels and container condition for anything that could interfere with aspiration or identification. Expected outcome: Calibration material is presented correctly. If correcting loading resolves calibration, complete verification and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Analyzer Readiness
steps.instructions: Confirm no reagent, waste, wash, fluidics, temperature, initialization, or other visible analyzer condition is preventing reliable calibration. Resolve external readiness issues before repeating calibration. Expected outcome: The analyzer is fully ready for calibration. If correcting an external readiness condition permits successful calibration, troubleshooting can stop after quality verification.

steps.title: 6. Inspect for Aspiration or Fluidic Problems
steps.instructions: Look for visible signs of bubbles, leakage, empty fluid containers, waste restrictions, loose accessible connections, or repeated aspiration-related messages. Do not proceed into internal fluidic disassembly. Expected outcome: No obvious external fluidics condition is affecting calibration. If an external fluid issue is corrected and calibration then succeeds, verify quality and stop.

steps.title: 7. Compare With Fresh or Known-Good Material
steps.instructions: When permitted by laboratory procedure, repeat using another suitable calibration material preparation or validated material source. This helps distinguish material-related failure from analyzer-related failure. Expected outcome: Calibration succeeds with suitable material. If the failure follows the original material, remove that material from use and stop.

steps.title: 8. Review Environmental Conditions
steps.instructions: Check for recent relocation, unusual room temperature conditions, power disturbances, analyzer shutdown, reagent replacement, or maintenance that coincided with the calibration problem. Correct only clearly identifiable external environmental issues. Expected outcome: No environmental condition remains that would reasonably interfere with stable analyzer operation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Calibration and Quality Verification
steps.instructions: Repeat calibration according to the laboratory-approved workflow after external causes are corrected. Complete required quality-control verification afterward. Expected outcome: Calibration completes successfully and subsequent quality checks are acceptable. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that calibration on the Abbott Alinity hq repeatedly failed to complete.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the calibration material container was improperly positioned and not presenting reliably for aspiration.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the container placement, confirmed calibration completed successfully, and documented that laboratory quality-control verification was required before patient testing resumed.

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Clot, Bubble, or Sample-Volume Error Repeats
description: Addresses repeated clot, bubble, or volume errors caused by specimen quality, handling, tube condition, aspiration presentation, consumables, or accessible fluidics.

steps.title: 1. Protect the Patient Specimen
steps.instructions: Stop repeated aspiration attempts on an irreplaceable or low-volume patient sample. Follow laboratory policy for alternate testing, recollection, or specimen handling. Identify whether the error affects a single specimen or multiple unrelated specimens. Expected outcome: The specimen is protected and a sample-specific versus analyzer-wide condition begins to be distinguished.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Specimen Carefully
steps.instructions: Check for visible clots, fibrin, bubbles, foam, inadequate volume, improper mixing, damaged tube, or unusual sample appearance. Clinical Engineering should not attempt to alter or salvage a specimen outside approved laboratory procedures. Expected outcome: Obvious specimen-related causes are identified. If the error is isolated to a compromised specimen and known-good specimens process normally, analyzer troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Tube Type and Presentation
steps.instructions: Confirm the specimen is in the laboratory-approved tube and is seated correctly in the rack or carrier. Check that labels, caps, adapters, or excessive label overlap are not affecting tube position. Expected outcome: The specimen is correctly presented to the analyzer. If repositioning resolves the problem, verify with a known-good sample and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check for Recurrent Errors Across Multiple Samples
steps.instructions: Review whether the same clot, bubble, or volume condition is occurring on multiple unrelated samples or only one collection source. A multi-sample pattern increases suspicion of an analyzer or fluid-path issue. Expected outcome: The scope of the problem is established.

steps.title: 5. Inspect the Accessible Sample Path
steps.instructions: Check the accessible aspiration and loading region for visible dried residue, contamination, label debris, obstruction, or other material that could interfere with sample access. Perform only approved external cleaning. Expected outcome: The accessible sample path is clean and unobstructed. If cleaning corrects the problem and repeat testing is normal, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Fluid and Waste Conditions
steps.instructions: Check required wash or diluent supplies, accessible connections, and waste status. Look for bubbles in externally visible fluid lines, leaks, kinks, or improperly installed containers. Do not open internal fluidic assemblies. Expected outcome: External fluidics are properly connected and free from obvious air entry or restrictions.

steps.title: 7. Substitute Known-Good External Items
steps.instructions: When appropriate, use a known-good rack, carrier, sample tube, or approved control material to determine whether the error follows an external item. Expected outcome: The faulty external condition is isolated. If known-good items process normally, remove the suspect item from use and stop.

steps.title: 8. Perform Approved Routine Cleaning if Indicated
steps.instructions: If the analyzer's normal approved cleaning workflow is appropriate for repeated sample-path contamination, ensure it is completed through the supported procedure. Do not improvise probe flushing or use unapproved cleaning materials. Expected outcome: Repeat errors stop after approved cleaning and the sample path operates normally.

steps.title: 9. Complete Functional and QC Verification
steps.instructions: Run appropriate known-good material and confirm normal aspiration, no recurrent clot/bubble/volume messages, and acceptable required QC. Expected outcome: The analyzer processes samples without recurrence and QC is acceptable. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported repeated bubble and insufficient-volume messages on the Abbott Alinity hq.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found one rack was not holding sample tubes fully upright, causing inconsistent sample presentation.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the damaged rack, verified normal processing with a known-good rack and control material, and confirmed required QC could proceed normally.

helpfulDetails: Whether one collection source was involved
Visible clot, fibrin, bubbles, or foam
Visible air or leaks in accessible lines

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Probe, Pipettor, or Aspiration Error Occurs
description: Addresses aspiration-related faults caused by sample condition, positioning, insufficient volume, obstruction, contamination, consumables, or accessible fluid-path problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Samples and Stop Repeated Aspiration Attempts
steps.instructions: Stop repeatedly presenting the same patient specimen if aspiration is unreliable. Preserve the specimen and use an alternate validated testing workflow when necessary. Document whether the failure affects one sample or all samples. Expected outcome: The specimen is protected and the scope of the aspiration problem is known.

steps.title: 2. Inspect the Sample
steps.instructions: Check the affected sample for insufficient volume, clotting, visible bubbles, foam, damaged tube, improper fill, unusual viscosity, or other obvious specimen conditions. Do not manipulate patient specimens outside laboratory-approved procedures. Expected outcome: The specimen appears suitable for aspiration. If the problem follows an unsuitable specimen and known-good samples process normally, analyzer troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Verify Tube Positioning
steps.instructions: Confirm the tube is correctly seated and properly loaded in the rack or carrier. Inspect labels, caps, and tube geometry for anything that could interfere with access. Expected outcome: The tube is correctly presented. If correcting loading resolves aspiration, verify with another sample and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Accessible Aspiration Area
steps.instructions: Observe the accessible probe or sample-entry region for dried material, visible contamination, an external obstruction, or obvious damage. Do not manually move the probe or enter the motion envelope while powered. Expected outcome: No external obstruction or visible damage is present. If approved cleaning of an accessible contaminated surface resolves the issue, verify function and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check Reagent, Wash, and Waste Conditions
steps.instructions: Verify required fluids are available and properly installed and that waste handling is not preventing normal fluidics operation. Inspect accessible tubing and containers for kinks, leaks, loose fittings, or obvious restrictions. Expected outcome: External fluid supplies and waste handling are normal. If correcting an external fluid condition restores aspiration, verify and stop.

steps.title: 6. Compare With a Known-Good Sample
steps.instructions: When laboratory policy permits, test a known-good control or specimen to determine whether the aspiration error follows the original sample or remains with the analyzer. Expected outcome: A sample-specific issue is distinguished from an analyzer-wide problem. If only the original sample fails, analyzer troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 7. Observe Whether the Error Is Position-Specific
steps.instructions: Determine whether failures consistently occur at one rack position, carrier, loading area, or type of sample presentation. Substitute a known-good rack or carrier if appropriate. Expected outcome: Any external accessory-related problem is isolated and corrected. If aspiration becomes reliable with a known-good accessory, remove the suspect accessory from use.

steps.title: 8. Perform Approved Cleaning or Maintenance Actions
steps.instructions: If laboratory or manufacturer-approved routine cleaning is indicated and within the Clinical Engineering support boundary, perform only the approved external or routine maintenance action. Do not dismantle internal probe assemblies or fluid manifolds. Expected outcome: Normal aspiration is restored. If errors continue, proceed to escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Process an appropriate known-good sample or control and confirm normal aspiration, transport, analysis initiation, and required QC performance. Expected outcome: Aspiration operates consistently without recurring fault. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported repeated aspiration errors on the Abbott Alinity hq during sample processing.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found one sample rack damaged and positioning tubes inconsistently beneath the aspiration path.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the damaged rack from use, verified normal aspiration with a known-good rack and control sample, and returned the analyzer for routine laboratory QC confirmation.

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Quality-Control Results Are Out of Range
description: Addresses out-of-range QC caused by control material, preparation, reagents, aspiration, calibration status, environmental conditions, or analytical instability.

steps.title: 1. Stop Affected Patient Testing
steps.instructions: Do not release patient results for affected tests while quality-control results are unacceptable. Follow laboratory policy for result review, alternate testing, and any required patient-result assessment. Identify which QC level, parameter, and direction of failure are involved. Expected outcome: Potentially unreliable patient results are contained and the QC problem is clearly defined.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the QC Failure Pattern
steps.instructions: Determine whether the problem affects one control level, one parameter, multiple parameters, or all QC material. Review whether the shift occurred suddenly or has been trending. Expected outcome: The scope and pattern of the QC failure are established.

steps.title: 3. Verify Control Material
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct QC material is being used and that storage, handling, mixing, preparation, and laboratory-defined use conditions are appropriate. Inspect the material for contamination, leakage, or insufficient volume. Expected outcome: QC material is suitable for testing. If questionable material is replaced and QC becomes acceptable, troubleshooting can stop after required confirmation.

steps.title: 4. Verify QC Identification and Assigned Information
steps.instructions: Confirm the control is correctly identified by the analyzer and that the laboratory is using the intended QC lot and associated configuration. Do not alter target data or acceptable ranges merely to make a failed result pass. Expected outcome: The correct QC material and associated laboratory configuration are confirmed.

steps.title: 5. Check Reagent and Consumable Status
steps.instructions: Review reagent recognition, inventory, recent reagent changes, empty or low consumables, wash status, and waste conditions. Inspect accessible reagent connections for obvious leakage, looseness, or installation problems. Expected outcome: Reagents and consumables are properly installed and available. If correcting an external reagent issue restores acceptable QC, troubleshooting can stop after confirmation.

steps.title: 6. Check Aspiration and Sample Presentation
steps.instructions: Verify the QC container is properly loaded and has adequate accessible volume. Look for bubbles, foam, tube damage, or repeated aspiration-related messages. Expected outcome: QC material can be aspirated consistently. If correcting presentation or replacing a compromised sample resolves QC, verify with an additional acceptable run and stop.

steps.title: 7. Review Calibration Status
steps.instructions: Determine whether a recent calibration, failed calibration, reagent change, prolonged shutdown, or maintenance event preceded the QC shift. Follow laboratory policy for any required calibration action. Expected outcome: Calibration status is appropriate and no unresolved calibration problem remains.

steps.title: 8. Compare With Fresh or Known-Good QC Material
steps.instructions: Use another properly prepared control sample when permitted. Compare results to determine whether the failure follows the QC material or remains with the analyzer. Expected outcome: A material-related issue is separated from analyzer-related instability. If fresh QC produces acceptable results consistently, remove the suspect material from use.

steps.title: 9. Review Environmental and Operational Conditions
steps.instructions: Check for recent relocation, room-condition changes, vibration, power events, fluid spills, prolonged idle time, or other environmental changes. Expected outcome: No external environmental condition remains likely to affect measurement performance.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final QC Verification
steps.instructions: Repeat the laboratory-required QC process after correcting any identified external cause. Expected outcome: Required QC results are acceptable and stable. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that Abbott Alinity hq QC results were repeatedly outside the laboratory's acceptable range.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the QC material contained visible bubbles and confirmed a properly prepared replacement control produced stable results.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the compromised control preparation from use, verified repeat QC was acceptable, and documented the analyzer's return to normal laboratory workflow.

helpfulDetails: QC results before and after correction

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Reagent Is Not Recognized or Inventory Is Incorrect
description: Addresses unrecognized reagents or inaccurate inventory caused by installation, identification, container condition, consumable status, connections, or inventory synchronization issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect Result Integrity
steps.instructions: Do not release patient results if reagent identification or available-volume status is unreliable. Follow the laboratory's alternate testing or downtime process until reagent status is verified. Identify which reagent or consumable is affected and whether the problem began after replacement. Expected outcome: Patient testing is protected and the affected reagent is identified.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Reported Inventory Condition
steps.instructions: Determine whether the analyzer shows the reagent as missing, unidentified, empty, expired, unavailable, incorrectly installed, or at an unexpected inventory level. Record the exact displayed status before making changes. Expected outcome: The failure is clearly documented. If the displayed inventory corrects after a normal screen refresh or approved workflow action and remains stable, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 3. Inspect the Reagent Container
steps.instructions: Verify the correct reagent is installed for the validated analyzer workflow. Inspect the container for obvious damage, leakage, deformation, incorrect orientation, or contamination. Confirm labeling and identification features are intact and readable. Expected outcome: The correct, intact reagent container is installed. If replacing a visibly damaged container resolves recognition, verify inventory and stop.

steps.title: 4. Verify Reagent Seating and Position
steps.instructions: Remove and reinstall the affected reagent only according to approved laboratory handling procedures. Make sure the container is fully seated in the intended position and any accessible connections are properly engaged. Do not force a container into position. Expected outcome: The reagent is properly seated and recognized. If inventory updates correctly, troubleshooting can stop after verifying normal readiness.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Reagent Connections
steps.instructions: Check accessible tubing, caps, connectors, pickup interfaces, and surrounding surfaces associated with the affected reagent for looseness, kinks, leakage, dried residue, or improper installation. Do not disconnect internal fluid lines. Expected outcome: Accessible reagent connections are intact and correctly installed. If correcting an external connection restores recognition or inventory, verify and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check Reagent Identification Information
steps.instructions: Confirm the installed container's identification information is intact and compatible with the laboratory's current inventory workflow. If appropriate, compare with a known-good reagent container from approved stock. Expected outcome: A known-good container is recognized normally. If the problem follows the original reagent container, remove that container from use and stop.

steps.title: 7. Allow Inventory to Update Normally
steps.instructions: After correcting installation, allow the analyzer to complete its normal reagent recognition or inventory update process. Avoid repeated removal and reinsertion that could complicate the inventory state. Expected outcome: The analyzer displays a stable and plausible reagent status. If the status remains correct through normal operation, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 8. Verify No Broader Consumable Problem Exists
steps.instructions: Check whether multiple reagents or consumables are simultaneously showing incorrect states. A multi-item issue may suggest a broader reader, configuration, software, or communication condition rather than multiple bad containers. Expected outcome: Either the issue remains isolated to one consumable or a broader pattern is identified for escalation.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the analyzer reaches the appropriate ready state and complete required laboratory quality checks before relying on the reagent for patient testing. Expected outcome: Reagent identification and inventory are stable, and required quality verification is satisfactory. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that a newly installed reagent was not recognized by the Abbott Alinity hq.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the reagent container not fully seated in its assigned position.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering reinstalled the reagent correctly, confirmed the analyzer recognized it and displayed the expected inventory state, and released the analyzer for laboratory quality verification.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or multiple reagents were affected

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Result Is Delayed, Missing, or Inconsistent
description: Addresses delayed, absent, or inconsistent results caused by sample problems, analyzer status, QC, communication, workflow, identification, or analytical instability.

steps.title: 1. Protect Patient Results
steps.instructions: Do not release or reconstruct questionable results outside approved laboratory procedures. If a result is missing, delayed, or inconsistent, ensure the specimen and patient identification remain controlled. Use an alternate validated analyzer when clinically necessary. Expected outcome: Patient care continues without relying on an unverified result.

steps.title: 2. Define the Result Problem Precisely
steps.instructions: Determine whether the result is delayed, never generated, generated but not displayed, present on the analyzer but missing downstream, or analytically inconsistent with repeat testing or clinical expectations. Record the sample identifier and timeline. Expected outcome: The issue is categorized as processing, analytical, display, or communication related.

steps.title: 3. Verify Sample Identification
steps.instructions: Confirm the correct specimen, barcode, rack position, and patient/order association were used. Inspect for duplicate, unreadable, damaged, or incorrectly placed labels. Expected outcome: The result is associated with the intended specimen and order. If an identification problem caused the apparent missing result, correct it only through approved laboratory procedures.

steps.title: 4. Check Analyzer Processing Status
steps.instructions: Determine whether the sample is waiting, actively processing, held, rejected, repeated, or stopped because of another analyzer condition. Review visible messages affecting the sample. Expected outcome: The sample's current processing state is understood. If a simple workflow hold is safely resolved and the result completes normally, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 5. Check for Sample Quality Problems
steps.instructions: Inspect the sample for clots, bubbles, inadequate volume, poor mixing, damaged tube, or other visible conditions that could delay or invalidate processing. Expected outcome: No obvious specimen condition explains the result problem, or the issue is correctly identified as sample-related.

steps.title: 6. Verify Reagent, Fluidics, and Waste Status
steps.instructions: Confirm the analyzer has the required reagents and fluids and is not operating under a wash, aspiration, waste, or fluidics fault. Expected outcome: The analyzer is mechanically and fluidically ready for reliable sample processing.

steps.title: 7. Review QC and Calibration Status
steps.instructions: Check whether current required laboratory QC and calibration status support reliable result generation. Do not treat a communication fix as sufficient if analytical quality is also in question. Expected outcome: Analytical readiness is verified. If QC is unacceptable, stop patient testing and troubleshoot the quality issue separately.

steps.title: 8. Determine Whether the Result Exists Locally
steps.instructions: If the result is missing downstream, determine whether it is present and complete on the analyzer. If present locally but absent from the LIS, focus troubleshooting on communication rather than repeating the test unnecessarily. Expected outcome: Analytical generation is separated from result-transmission failure.

steps.title: 9. Check LIS and Network Communication
steps.instructions: Review analyzer communication status and determine whether other results are transmitting normally. Coordinate with IT or the laboratory interface team when multiple results or systems are affected. Expected outcome: The downstream result path is functioning or an infrastructure fault is identified for escalation.

steps.title: 10. Evaluate Inconsistent Results Carefully
steps.instructions: For inconsistent values, determine whether the discrepancy follows one specimen, one sample preparation, one parameter, or multiple unrelated samples. Use laboratory-approved repeat testing, alternate analyzer comparison, or control material as appropriate. Clinical Engineering should not interpret patient results clinically. Expected outcome: A specimen-specific issue is distinguished from analyzer instability.

steps.title: 11. Review Recent Changes
steps.instructions: Check for recent reagent replacement, calibration, maintenance, software or network changes, analyzer restart, relocation, or power events. Expected outcome: Any relevant change is identified and evaluated before deeper troubleshooting.

steps.title: 12. Perform Final End-to-End Verification
steps.instructions: Use approved laboratory material or a suitable test workflow to confirm normal sample processing, result generation, consistency, display, and downstream transmission. Expected outcome: Results are generated consistently and arrive at the intended destination without abnormal delay. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that results from the Abbott Alinity hq were completing on the analyzer but were intermittently missing from the LIS.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found an unstable external network connection causing intermittent result transmission.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the network connection and verified multiple approved test transmissions reached the intended downstream system while analyzer QC remained acceptable.

helpfulDetails: Whether result was delayed, missing, or inconsistent

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Sample, Rack, or Carrier Is Not Detected
description: Addresses missed sample, rack, or carrier detection caused by positioning, identification, loading, obstruction, accessory condition, or external sensor-path issues.

steps.title: 1. Protect Specimen Workflow
steps.instructions: Do not continue repeatedly loading patient specimens into an unreliable transport or detection path. Route testing through an alternate validated workflow if necessary. Identify whether the problem affects one specimen, one rack or carrier, or all loaded samples. Expected outcome: Patient specimens remain controlled and the scope of the detection problem is established.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Failure
steps.instructions: Determine whether the analyzer fails to recognize the sample entirely, detects the carrier but not the tube, rejects one position, fails intermittently, or stops transport. Document any displayed message or indicator. Expected outcome: The failure is reproducible and clearly defined. If the issue cannot be reproduced and normal detection is verified repeatedly, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 3. Inspect Sample and Tube Positioning
steps.instructions: Verify the sample tube is properly seated, upright where required, and appropriate for the laboratory's validated Alinity hq workflow. Check for damaged tubes, loose caps, excessive labels, peeling labels, or label placement that could interfere with handling or identification. Expected outcome: The sample is correctly positioned and physically suitable for transport and detection. If correcting tube placement resolves detection, verify with another sample and stop.

steps.title: 4. Inspect the Rack or Carrier
steps.instructions: Examine the affected rack or carrier for cracks, contamination, deformation, worn identification features, foreign material, or improper loading. Compare it with a known-good rack or carrier when available. Expected outcome: The carrier is intact and properly loaded. If a known-good carrier works normally while the original does not, remove the defective accessory from use and stop.

steps.title: 5. Check the Loading and Transport Area
steps.instructions: Inspect accessible sample-loading and transport surfaces for dried material, debris, misplaced tubes, label fragments, or other obstructions. Clean only accessible areas using approved procedures. Do not reach into moving mechanisms. Expected outcome: The sample path is clear and accessible surfaces are clean. If removing an external obstruction restores detection, verify normal transport and stop.

steps.title: 6. Verify Barcode and Identification Conditions
steps.instructions: If detection appears related to sample identification, inspect barcode quality, orientation, wrinkles, contrast, and placement. Try a known-good properly labeled specimen or laboratory-approved test item to distinguish a sample-label problem from an analyzer problem. Expected outcome: A known-good identification item is recognized normally. If only the original label fails, correct the specimen-identification issue and stop.

steps.title: 7. Compare Multiple Positions and Carriers
steps.instructions: Test another known-good rack or carrier and, if practical, another sample position. Determine whether the failure follows the specimen, follows the carrier, or remains at the analyzer. Do not use patient specimens for unnecessary repeated testing. Expected outcome: The affected element is isolated. If replacing an external carrier or correcting loading resolves the condition, verify normal operation and stop.

steps.title: 8. Verify Analyzer Readiness and Settings
steps.instructions: Confirm the analyzer is in the correct operating state to accept specimens and that no visible control, paused workflow, or laboratory-approved setting is preventing sample processing. Do not modify restricted configuration merely to force detection. Expected outcome: The analyzer is configured and ready for normal specimen loading. If restoring the correct operating state resolves detection, troubleshooting can stop.

steps.title: 9. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Run a known-good laboratory-approved sample or control through the normal loading path and confirm that detection, identification, transport, and processing begin normally. Expected outcome: Sample and carrier detection function consistently. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported that the Abbott Alinity hq intermittently failed to detect samples loaded in one rack.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the affected rack damaged and confirmed a known-good rack was detected normally.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering removed the damaged rack from service, verified normal sample detection with a known-good rack, and returned the analyzer for laboratory quality verification.

helpfulDetails: Whether one or all samples were affected

title: Abbott Alinity hq Hematology Analyzer - Wash, Waste, or Fluidics System Fault Occurs
description: Addresses wash, waste, and fluidics faults caused by empty supplies, full waste, poor connections, kinks, leaks, air, blockage, or installation problems.

steps.title: 1. Protect Testing and Inspect for Leakage
steps.instructions: Stop patient testing if wash, waste, or fluid handling is unreliable. Inspect around the analyzer before touching anything. If there is significant leakage, unknown chemical exposure, electrical wetting, or a biohazard spill beyond normal containment, remove the analyzer from service and follow facility safety procedures. Expected outcome: No uncontrolled hazard is present, or the analyzer is safely removed from service.

steps.title: 2. Confirm the Exact Fluidics Fault
steps.instructions: Determine whether the issue involves wash solution, diluent, another reagent fluid, waste collection, drainage, fluid transfer, or a general fluidics status. Record the exact displayed message and when it occurs. Expected outcome: The affected fluid pathway is identified.

steps.title: 3. Check External Fluid Supplies
steps.instructions: Verify required wash and other externally managed fluids are present, correctly installed, and not obviously empty or improperly connected. Inspect containers for damage, leakage, collapsed walls, loose caps, or incorrect placement. Expected outcome: Required fluids are available and properly installed. If correcting a supply installation clears the fault, verify operation and stop.

steps.title: 4. Check Waste Collection
steps.instructions: Inspect the accessible waste container or waste connection used by the installation. Confirm waste is not full, disconnected, kinked, improperly positioned, or otherwise preventing normal drainage. Use proper PPE for potentially biohazardous waste. Expected outcome: Waste can be handled normally. If correcting a full or improperly connected waste setup resolves the fault, verify and stop.

steps.title: 5. Inspect Accessible Tubing and Connections
steps.instructions: Look for pinched tubing, kinks, loose fittings, obvious air gaps, wet connections, dried residue, or tubing pulled from its intended routing. Do not disconnect or open internal fluid manifolds. Expected outcome: Accessible fluid connections are intact and unobstructed. If correcting an external kink or loose approved connection resolves the problem, verify and stop.

steps.title: 6. Check for Recent Consumable Changes
steps.instructions: Determine whether the fault began after fluid-container replacement, waste service, cleaning, relocation, or maintenance. Recheck the installation of anything recently handled. Expected outcome: Any installation-related cause is corrected. If normal fluidics resume, troubleshooting can stop after verification.

steps.title: 7. Inspect for External Obstruction or Drainage Problems
steps.instructions: Where the system uses facility drainage or external waste routing, verify the accessible route is not compressed, elevated incorrectly, or visibly blocked. Coordinate with facilities when a building drainage issue is suspected. Expected outcome: External drainage or waste infrastructure is functioning normally.

steps.title: 8. Perform the Supported Fluidics Recovery
steps.instructions: If permitted within the normal approved workflow, allow the analyzer to perform its supported prime, wash, or fluidics recovery process. Do not repeatedly run recovery cycles when the system continues to fault. Expected outcome: Fluid flow recovers and the analyzer reaches normal ready status. If not, escalate.

steps.title: 9. Check for Continued Leakage or Air
steps.instructions: Observe accessible areas during recovery for recurring bubbles, leakage, poor fluid pickup, or waste backup. Expected outcome: Fluid movement appears stable without leakage or persistent air introduction.

steps.title: 10. Perform Final Functional Verification
steps.instructions: Confirm the fluidics fault has cleared, the analyzer reaches ready status, and required QC passes before patient testing resumes. Expected outcome: Wash, waste, and fluidics operation are stable and QC is acceptable. The issue is resolved and troubleshooting can stop.

CCR.Complaint: Laboratory staff reported a recurring waste-system fault on the Abbott Alinity hq.
CCR.Cause: Clinical Engineering found the accessible waste tubing kinked behind the analyzer and restricting drainage.
CCR.Resolution: Clinical Engineering corrected the tubing routing, confirmed normal waste flow and fault clearance, and verified the analyzer was ready for laboratory QC before patient testing resumed.
